rv.q: The script has a tendency to swerve quickly from one idea or exchange to the next, making the narrative feel scattered.
It’s difficult to say why a production that ended in a wildly enthusiastic standing ovation left me comparatively underwhelmed.

This is an oddly listless and unsatisfying evening, only getting close to the tension of a nail-biting match in its final, dynamically staged game, when Graham’s stylised movements and the nifty use of a light-up floor deliver a cohesive, slick stage language for the beautiful game.
It's impossible not to be moved by this production; it's an extraordinary piece of theatre.
The performances are authentic and passionate, and at times, genuinely moving.
The Ladies Football Club is a joyous production, combining witty dialogue with energetic movement.

cn.t: Mixed reception for this WWI women's football drama—some find it humorous and moving, others feel it never quite finds its feet. Ensemble movement wins praise; familiarity with the story and uneven storytelling divide critics.
